prompt: In Connecticut, a driver 21 or older has an 'elevated blood alcohol content' at what BAC?
explanation: Connecticut law defines an elevated blood alcohol content as 0.08% or more for drivers of ordinary (non-commercial) vehicles. You can still be convicted below 0.08 if you are impaired.

prompt: Connecticut's zero-tolerance law for drivers under 21 applies at what blood alcohol content?
explanation: Drivers under 21 face penalties for any measurable alcohol, defined as .02% or more. The 0.08 limit applies to adults.

prompt: A 19-year-old is stopped while driving in a store parking lot and tests at .03% BAC. What happens under Connecticut's zero-tolerance law?
choices: Nothing, because the zero-tolerance law applies only on public roads
Nothing, because .03% is below the adult limit
The license is suspended for at least 45 days and an ignition interlock is required to get it back
Only a written warning is issued for a first offense
explanation: Zero tolerance covers .02% or more on public roads and private property. A result of .02% or higher brings a suspension of at least 45 days and an ignition interlock device (IID) for at least one year.

prompt: What is Connecticut's elevated blood alcohol content level for a person operating a commercial motor vehicle?
explanation: For commercial motor vehicle operators, an elevated blood alcohol content is 0.04% or more, half the 0.08% level for other drivers.

prompt: If you are arrested for DUI in Connecticut and refuse a blood, breath or urine test, what happens to your license?
choices: Nothing, as long as you are not convicted
It is suspended for at least 45 days, and an ignition interlock is required for at least one year after
It is suspended for 7 days only
It is suspended only if you are under 21
explanation: Regardless of age, refusing the test means a suspension of at least 45 days. You must then install an ignition interlock device for at least one year to get your license back.

prompt: A 30-year-old driver is arrested for DUI and fails the chemical test. According to the Connecticut manual, how long must an ignition interlock device be used, at minimum, to get the license back?
choices: No interlock is required for a first failure
explanation: Failing the test brings a suspension of at least 45 days, and the IID is required for at least six months, longer with prior offenses. Refusing the test or being under 21 means at least one year with the IID.

prompt: What fine range does Connecticut law set for a first DUI conviction?
explanation: A first conviction carries a $500 to $1,000 fine, up to six months in jail, and a 45-day suspension. That is followed by one year of driving only with an ignition interlock. $1,000 to $4,000 is the range for a second offense.

prompt: According to the Connecticut manual, after how many drinks could a person under 21 be considered impaired?
explanation: The manual warns that in Connecticut, people under 21 could be considered impaired after only one drink of alcohol.

prompt: A 17-year-old is charged with driving under the influence in Connecticut. Can the teen be treated as a youthful offender?
choices: Yes, any driver under 18 can be
No, DUI is one of the offenses excluded from youthful offender status
Yes, if it is a first offense
explanation: Someone under 18 who commits DUI, negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, or evading responsibility in a crash with death or serious injury cannot be treated as a youthful offender.

prompt: What is the minimum age to get a learner's permit in Connecticut?
explanation: You must be at least 16 to get a Connecticut learner's permit, and you must pass both a vision test and a 25-question knowledge test.

prompt: How many questions must you answer correctly to pass Connecticut's 25-question learner's permit knowledge test?
explanation: The knowledge test has 25 questions and you need 20 correct answers (80%) to pass.

prompt: How long is a Connecticut learner's permit valid?
choices: Until you get a license or 2 years from issue, whichever comes first
explanation: The permit is valid until you obtain a driver's license or for 2 years from the date it is issued, whichever comes first.

prompt: A 16-year-old completes driver education at a licensed commercial driving school. How long must the teen hold a learner's permit before taking the road test?
explanation: Teens who complete driver education at a commercial driving school or high school must wait 120 days after the permit is issued. All other applicants, including home-trained teens, must wait 180 days.

prompt: A 16-year-old is home trained by a parent. How long must the teen hold the learner's permit before the road test?
explanation: Applicants who do not complete driver education through a commercial driving school or a secondary school must wait 180 days after the learner's permit is issued.

prompt: How long must a first-time driver aged 18 or older hold a Connecticut learner's permit before taking the road test?
explanation: Applicants 18 or older must obtain and hold a learner's permit for at least 90 days before taking the road test.

prompt: How many hours of behind-the-wheel, on-the-road training must 16- and 17-year-old applicants complete in Connecticut?
explanation: All 16- and 17-year-old applicants need at least 40 hours of behind-the-wheel training. Any mix of driving school and home training counts. The manual recommends 100 hours before driving solo.

prompt: Which person may serve as a qualified trainer for a Connecticut learner's permit holder?
choices: A 19-year-old sibling licensed for three years
A 45-year-old parent licensed for 20 years with no suspension in the last four years
A 25-year-old friend whose license was suspended last year
explanation: A qualified trainer must be at least 20, have held a license for four or more consecutive years, and have had no suspension during the four years before training.

prompt: Where must the person supervising a Connecticut learner's permit holder sit?
choices: In the back seat directly behind the driver
In the front passenger seat next to the learner
In the front seat only on highways
explanation: The person giving instruction must sit in the front passenger seat and be alert and ready to take control of the vehicle.

prompt: A 16-year-old with a learner's permit wants to drive two classmates to school with a qualified trainer in the front seat. Is this allowed?
choices: Yes, if the trainer is over 20
Yes, if the classmates wear seat belts
No, teen permit holders may not carry passengers other than the instructor or trainer (and parents)
explanation: For the entire time a 16- or 17-year-old holds a permit, the only passengers allowed are a licensed driving instructor (and those with the instructor) or one qualified trainer. Parents or a legal guardian may also come along.

prompt: Who must complete an 8-hour Safe Driving Practices course before getting a Connecticut license?
choices: Anyone, at any age, who has never held a Connecticut license and does not hold a valid license from another state
explanation: Connecticut law requires anyone, regardless of age, who has not held a Connecticut license or a valid out-of-state license to take the 8-hour Safe Driving Practices course.

prompt: How much training must a parent or legal guardian of a 16- or 17-year-old permit holder complete in Connecticut?
choices: Two hours of instruction with the teen
explanation: A parent or legal guardian must complete two hours of instruction with the teen on teen driving laws and dangers. It is part of the eight-hour course.

prompt: Since January 1, 2026, what must every Connecticut learner's permit applicant complete before the knowledge test?
choices: A free online Connecticut Work Zone Safety Course
explanation: Starting January 1, 2026, anyone applying for a learner's permit must complete the free online Connecticut Work Zone Safety Course and bring the completion certificate to the test.
ref: CT DMV knowledge and vision test page (portal.ct.gov)

prompt: If you fail the Connecticut knowledge test, how long must you wait before retaking it?
choices: You may retake it the same day
explanation: If you fail the knowledge test you must wait seven days and pay the $40 fee again to reschedule.
ref: CT DMV knowledge and vision test page (portal.ct.gov)

prompt: During the first six months with a license, which passengers may a 16-year-old Connecticut driver carry?
choices: Only a licensed driving instructor, parents or legal guardian, or one qualified adult 20 or older
Anyone, as long as an adult is present
explanation: For the first six months, the only passengers allowed are a licensed driving instructor, the teen's parents or legal guardian (one must be licensed), or one person 20 or older licensed for four or more years with no recent suspension.

prompt: A 17-year-old has had a license for eight months. Who may the teen now carry as passengers, in addition to those allowed in the first six months?
choices: Members of the teen's immediate family
explanation: During months seven through twelve, the only additional passengers allowed are members of the driver's immediate family. Friends are not allowed until the license is one year old.

prompt: During what hours may 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers NOT drive in Connecticut, unless an exception applies?
explanation: The teen curfew is 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., unless the teen is traveling for employment, school, religious activities, or medical necessity, or is an assigned Safe Ride Program driver.

prompt: A 16-year-old wants to drive home from a friend's birthday party at 11:45 p.m. Is this allowed under Connecticut's curfew?
choices: Yes, if a parent gives permission by phone
Yes, because it is a trip home
No, social trips are not a curfew exception
Yes, if the teen drives under the speed limit
explanation: The 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. curfew allows exceptions only for employment, school, religious activities, medical necessity, Safe Ride drivers, and volunteer emergency responders. A social event is not an exception.

prompt: Which rule applies to Connecticut learner's permit holders and 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers?
choices: They may carry more passengers than seat belts if traveling short distances
They may not carry more passengers than the number of seat belts in the vehicle
They may drive a vanpool vehicle with a parent aboard
They may use a hands-free phone
explanation: Permit holders and 16- and 17-year-old drivers may not carry more passengers than there are seat belts. They also may not drive vanpool or public passenger vehicles or use any cell phone.

prompt: What is the license suspension for a 16- or 17-year-old's first conviction for violating Connecticut's teen passenger or curfew restrictions?
explanation: A first GDL violation brings a 30-day suspension and a $175 restoration fee. A second violation brings 6 months or until age 18, whichever is longer.

prompt: A 17-year-old is convicted of driving 20 mph or more over the speed limit for the first time. What suspension does Connecticut impose?
explanation: For drivers under 18, a first conviction for speeding 20 mph or more over the limit brings a 60-day suspension. It is 90 days for a second and 6 months for a third.

prompt: What is the suspension for a 16-year-old's first conviction for using a cell phone or texting while driving in Connecticut?
explanation: A first cell phone or texting conviction for a 16- or 17-year-old brings a 30-day suspension and a $175 restoration fee. It is 90 days for a second and 6 months for a third.

prompt: A 16-year-old is convicted of reckless driving for the first time. How long is the license suspended?
explanation: For 16- and 17-year-olds, a first reckless driving or street racing conviction brings a 6-month suspension. Later offenses bring 1 year.

prompt: In Connecticut, a driver aged 24 or younger must complete the operator retraining program after how many moving violations?
explanation: Anyone 24 or younger with two or more moving or suspension violations must complete the DMV-certified operator retraining program. Drivers 25 and older must attend after three or more.

prompt: A 40-year-old Connecticut driver must attend the operator retraining program after how many moving violation convictions?
explanation: A motorist 25 or older with three or more such convictions must attend and pass the operator retraining program.

prompt: After completing Connecticut's operator retraining program, what happens if you get another moving violation within three years?
choices: A license suspension of at least 30 days
You must retake the knowledge test
explanation: An additional moving violation within three years of completing operator retraining results in a license suspension of at least 30 days.

prompt: What are Connecticut's minimum liability insurance limits?
explanation: Connecticut requires at least $25,000 per person and $50,000 per accident for bodily injury, plus $25,000 for property damage.

prompt: Your car insurance lapses and you ignore the Connecticut DMV's warning notice. What happens?
choices: Nothing until you have a crash
explanation: Connecticut requires continuous insurance on any registered vehicle. If you do not respond to the warning notice, the registration is suspended, and the vehicle cannot legally be driven on a public highway.

prompt: You are an adult driver stopped at a red light in Connecticut. May you pick up your hand-held phone to make a call?
choices: Yes, because the vehicle is stopped
Yes, if the call is under one minute
No, the ban also applies when temporarily stopped for traffic or a signal
Yes, if you are on speaker
explanation: Connecticut prohibits using hand-held phones and mobile electronic devices while driving, including when temporarily stopped for traffic, road conditions, or a sign or signal.

prompt: When may an adult Connecticut driver legally use a hand-held phone without an emergency?
choices: While parked safely on the side or shoulder of the highway
While waiting at a stop sign
explanation: You may use a phone or mobile electronic device if you are parked safely on the side or shoulder of the highway. Being stopped in traffic still counts as driving.

prompt: Which type of phone use is allowed for a 30-year-old Connecticut driver while driving?
choices: Holding the phone to the ear
Reading email at a red light
explanation: Drivers 18 and older may use only hands-free mobile phone accessories. Hand-held use and texting are banned.

prompt: May a 17-year-old Connecticut driver use a hands-free phone while driving?
choices: Yes, hands-free is legal for everyone
No, drivers under 18 may not use any cell phone, even hands-free, except in an emergency
Yes, with a parent in the car
explanation: Drivers who are 16 or 17 may not use any type of cell phone or mobile electronic device, including hands-free devices. The only exception is an emergency call.

prompt: What is the fine for a first violation of Connecticut's hand-held phone and texting law?
explanation: Fines are $200 for a first violation, $375 for a second, and $625 for a third or later. Fines are doubled in work zones.

prompt: In Connecticut, when may a driver of any age use a cell phone while driving?
choices: To call an emergency response operator, hospital, doctor's office, ambulance company, or fire or police department in an emergency
To answer a call from a parent
To use a navigation app by hand
To send a short text at a stop sign
explanation: Any driver may use a phone in an emergency to contact an emergency operator, hospital, physician's office, health clinic, ambulance company, or fire or police department.

prompt: What happens to distracted driving fines if you are convicted of using a hand-held phone in a Connecticut work zone?
choices: They are replaced by a warning
explanation: Distracted driving fines are doubled for anyone convicted of illegally using a hand-held phone or mobile electronic device while driving in a work zone.

prompt: Who is required to wear a seat belt in a Connecticut vehicle?
explanation: In Connecticut it is illegal to drive or to be a passenger without wearing a safety belt. The driver and each unbelted passenger can be cited.

prompt: Under Connecticut law, a child who is under 2 years old or weighs less than 30 pounds must ride in what type of seat?
choices: A forward-facing seat with a lap belt
A rear-facing car seat with a 5-point harness
The rear seat with an adult seat belt
explanation: Children under 2, or under 30 pounds regardless of age, must use a rear-facing-only seat or rear-facing convertible seat with a 5-point harness.

prompt: A 6-year-old weighs 50 pounds. Under Connecticut's child restraint law, what may the child use?
choices: A 5-point harness or a booster seat
No restraint in the back seat
explanation: Children aged 5 to 8, or weighing 40 to 60 pounds, must use a 5-point harness or a booster seat. A booster or seat belt is allowed only at age 8 and 60 pounds or more.

prompt: A child is 18 months old but weighs 33 pounds. Which Connecticut restraint rule applies?
choices: The weight rule, so a forward-facing seat
The more restrictive rule, so a rear-facing car seat
explanation: If a child's age and weight fall in two categories, the more restrictive requirement applies. A child under two must ride rear-facing even if heavier than 30 pounds.

prompt: Under Connecticut law, where may a rear-facing child seat NOT be placed?
choices: In the middle of the back seat
In the front seat of a vehicle with an active passenger-side airbag
explanation: Connecticut law prohibits placing a rear-facing child restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a working passenger-side airbag.

prompt: Unless a higher limit is posted for a multi-lane limited-access highway, what is the maximum speed on Connecticut highways?
explanation: Connecticut law sets 55 mph as the maximum on highways other than the designated multi-lane limited-access highways, where up to 65 mph may be set.

prompt: What is the highest speed limit Connecticut may set on a multiple-lane, limited-access highway?
explanation: The Office of the State Traffic Administration may establish a speed limit not exceeding 65 mph on multiple-lane, limited-access highways.

prompt: What is the minimum speed on a Connecticut limited-access divided highway, unless slower is needed for safety?
explanation: No one may drive slower than 40 mph on a limited-access divided highway, except when a reduced speed is necessary for safety, in an emergency, or as directed by law or an officer.

prompt: The Connecticut manual's "four-second sight-distance rule" is used to check what?
choices: Whether you are following a car too closely
Whether you are driving too fast for how far ahead you can see
How long to signal before turning
How long to stop at a stop sign
explanation: Pick a fixed object as far ahead as you can clearly see and count four seconds. If you reach it before you finish, you are driving too fast for your sight distance.

prompt: According to the Connecticut manual, what is the minimum following time behind a truck?
explanation: Never follow a truck at a time interval of less than three seconds. Following closely means you cannot see around it and the driver cannot see you.

prompt: What following distance does the Connecticut manual recommend behind a motorcycle?
choices: 3 to 4 seconds or more in wet conditions
explanation: Allow a 3- to 4-second following distance behind a motorcyclist, or more in wet conditions. Motorcycles can stop quickly.

prompt: According to the Connecticut manual, how large an opening in traffic do you need to merge or change lanes?
explanation: You need an opening of about four seconds to merge. If you move into the middle of a four-second gap, you and the car behind you each have two seconds.

prompt: In Connecticut, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
explanation: Do not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

prompt: Under Connecticut law in effect since October 1, 2025, how close to a stop sign may you park?
explanation: The law now bars parking within 30 feet of a stop sign or yield sign. The March 2023 manual still lists the older 25-foot rule for stop signs.

prompt: With no marked parking space or curb extension, how far from an intersection or the approach to a marked crosswalk must a parked car be in Connecticut?
explanation: Since October 1, 2025, no vehicle may remain parked within 30 feet of an intersection or the approach to a marked crosswalk. It is 20 feet where there is a curb extension, and a marked parking space is allowed.

prompt: When you parallel park next to a curb in Connecticut, how close must your wheels be to the curb?
explanation: You may not park more than one foot from the curb. Park as close to it as you can.

prompt: Connecticut law requires a turn signal to be given continuously for at least how far before turning?
explanation: A signal of intention to turn must be given continuously during at least the last 100 feet before the turn. The manual also advises signaling at least three seconds ahead.

prompt: How many seconds before you turn or change lanes does the Connecticut manual advise you to signal?
choices: Only once you begin the turn
explanation: Try to signal at least three seconds before you make your move. Do not signal so early that other drivers think you are turning at an earlier street or driveway.

prompt: May you turn right on a red light in Connecticut?
choices: Yes, after a full stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
Yes, without stopping if no one is coming
explanation: You may turn right on red after coming to a full stop and checking that no traffic is coming and no sign prohibits the turn. Watch for pedestrians.

prompt: You approach an intersection where the traffic lights are not working. What does Connecticut law require?
choices: Slow down and proceed if clear
Stop as though the intersection were controlled by a stop sign
Yield only to traffic on the left
Proceed if you are on the larger road
explanation: State law requires a driver at an intersection with an inoperative stop light to stop as though it were controlled by a stop sign.

prompt: Traffic is backed up on the far side of a green-light intersection. Under Connecticut law, what should you do?
choices: Enter the intersection so you are ready to go
Wait until there is room on the other side before entering
Enter if the light just turned green
explanation: Drivers may not enter an intersection unless there is room on the other side for their vehicle. This is known as 'blocking the box' and can lead to a ticket.

prompt: Connecticut law requires your headlights to be on during which of these times?
choices: From a half-hour after sunset to a half-hour before sunrise, and whenever it is raining, snowing or foggy
Only when it is fully dark
explanation: Lights are required from a half-hour after sunset to a half-hour before sunrise, whenever people and vehicles are not clearly visible 500 feet ahead, and during any precipitation.

prompt: It starts to rain lightly and you turn on your windshield wipers. What does Connecticut law require?
explanation: The Connecticut manual says: if you turn on your wipers, turn on your headlights. It's the law. Never drive with only parking lights on.

prompt: Under Connecticut law, you must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within how many feet?
explanation: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet. The manual describes this as about a one-block distance.

prompt: Under Connecticut law, you must switch to low beams when following another vehicle within how many feet?
explanation: When approaching another vehicle from the rear within 300 feet, you may not use your high beams. The 500-foot rule is for oncoming traffic.

prompt: At a HAWK pedestrian signal, the light is flashing red. What must you do?
choices: Stop, then proceed once pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk
Stop and wait for a green light
explanation: A flashing red HAWK signal means it is about to deactivate. Drivers must stop but may proceed when pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk. A solid red means stop and stay stopped.

prompt: When your direction of travel has fewer than three lanes, what does Connecticut law require?
choices: Drive in any lane you choose
Drive in the right lane except when passing (or preparing to turn or exit left)
Drive in the left lane at highway speeds
Drive in the center of the road
explanation: When your direction of travel has fewer than three lanes, Connecticut law requires you to drive in the right lane except when passing. You may move left to make a left turn or a left exit.

prompt: In a Connecticut no-passing zone marked with a double yellow line, may you cross the line to pass a slow-moving bicycle?
choices: Yes, if you can see far enough ahead to pass safely
Only if the cyclist waves you by
Only if the bicycle is going slower than 10 mph
explanation: State law allows passing slow-moving vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals, and parked or standing vehicles in no-passing zones, if you can see far enough ahead to pass safely.

prompt: A bus stopped at the curb ahead of you signals that it is pulling back into your lane. What does Connecticut law require?
choices: Speed up to pass it first
Yield the right-of-way to the bus
Honk to warn the bus driver
explanation: Drivers are required to yield the right-of-way to a bus traveling in the same direction when the bus signals appropriately.

prompt: During what period are studded tires allowed in Connecticut?
explanation: Studded tires are permitted in Connecticut from November 15 through April 30.

prompt: You drive off after a snowstorm without clearing the snow from your car's roof. What is the Connecticut fine if the snow poses a threat?
explanation: Drivers must clear accumulated ice and snow, including from the hood, trunk and roof. The fine is $75, or $200 to $1,000 if snow or ice flies off and causes injury or damage.

prompt: In Connecticut, speeding or endangering a highway worker in a work zone can bring a fine of up to how much?
explanation: Speeding, disobeying traffic control devices, using an improper lane, or endangering a highway worker in a work zone can bring fines up to $1,000. It can also mean license points and retraining.

prompt: How much space must you leave when passing a bicyclist in Connecticut?
explanation: Slow down and pass only when you can leave at least three feet between your vehicle and the bicycle, including any load or trailer.

prompt: Under Connecticut's Vulnerable User's Law, which of these is considered a vulnerable user?
explanation: Vulnerable users include pedestrians, bicyclists, wheelchair users, people riding or driving animals, highway workers, garbage trucks, tank vehicles, mail vehicles, and express delivery carriers. Drivers must allow three feet when passing.

prompt: What happens to the fine in Connecticut for failing to yield the right-of-way to a bicyclist?
choices: It is replaced by a warning
explanation: Fines are doubled for failure to yield the right-of-way to a bicyclist.

prompt: Under Connecticut law, which bicyclists are required to wear a helmet?
explanation: Bicyclists under 16 must wear a helmet. Riders 16 and older should consider wearing one.

prompt: An ice cream truck ahead has its lights flashing and its stop arm out. What does Connecticut law require?
choices: Stop at least 10 feet from the truck, then pass at no more than 5 mph while yielding to pedestrians
Stop and wait until the stop arm is pulled in
Honk and pass on the left
explanation: When approaching or overtaking an ice cream truck with flashing lights and its stop arm extended, stop at least 10 feet away. Then you may pass at a reasonable speed up to 5 mph, yielding to pedestrians.

prompt: After stopping for an ice cream truck with its stop arm out, at what maximum speed may you pass it in Connecticut?
explanation: After stopping, you may pass the truck at a reasonable speed, up to 5 mph. You must yield to any pedestrian crossing to or from the truck.

prompt: When are you NOT required to stop for an ice cream truck displaying its flashing lights and stop arm in Connecticut?
choices: When it is in another lane separated by a safety island or physical barrier
When you are approaching it from the opposite direction on an undivided road
When you are driving slower than 10 mph
explanation: You must stop at least 10 feet from the front or back of the truck whether you are approaching or overtaking it. The only exception is a truck in another lane separated by a safety island or physical barrier.

prompt: You are approaching a horse and rider on a Connecticut road. What is illegal?
choices: Sounding your horn or making loud noises
explanation: It is illegal to sound your horn or make loud or unusual noises when approaching or passing a horse. Reduce speed, or stop if needed.

prompt: An ambulance with flashing lights and siren has just passed you. How closely may you follow it under Connecticut law?
explanation: A driver following an ambulance that is using flashing lights or a siren may not follow more closely than 100 feet.

prompt: You are in the middle of an intersection when you hear a siren behind you. What does the Connecticut manual say to do?
choices: Drive through the intersection, then pull over to the right and stop
Back up out of the intersection
explanation: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge and stopping. If you are in an intersection, drive through it before you pull over. Stay stopped until it passes.

prompt: Under Connecticut's Move Over Law, what must you do when any vehicle is pulled over on the road ahead?
choices: Nothing unless it has flashing lights
Slow down below the posted limit and move over one lane when safe
explanation: When any vehicle is pulled over on a highway or road, slow down below the posted speed limit and move over one lane whenever it is safe.

prompt: A school bus is stopped ahead with flashing red lights. Under Connecticut law, how far from the bus must you stop?
explanation: Stop at least 10 feet from the front or rear of a school bus showing flashing red lights, and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing.

prompt: On a Connecticut road, a school bus with flashing red lights is stopped on the opposite side of a median barrier. What should you do?
choices: Proceed with caution; you do not have to stop
explanation: You are not required to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a highway separated by a median, safety island, or physical barrier. On an undivided road, you must stop.

prompt: What is the Connecticut fine for a first offense of passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights?
explanation: Failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights brings a $450 fine for a first offense. Later offenses bring $500 to $1,000, up to 30 days in jail, or both.

prompt: A pedestrian stands at the curb at a crosswalk and raises a hand toward oncoming traffic. What does Connecticut law require?
choices: Nothing until the pedestrian steps into the road
Slow or stop and yield to the pedestrian
Honk to let them know you are coming
explanation: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian who steps to the curb at a crosswalk entrance and signals intent by raising a hand toward traffic. This applies at marked or unmarked crosswalks.

prompt: A car in the next lane has stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross. What does Connecticut law say?
choices: You may not overtake and pass the stopped vehicle
Pass only if the pedestrian is in the other lane
explanation: No driver approaching from the rear may pass a vehicle that has stopped at a marked or unmarked crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross.

prompt: In Connecticut, which pedestrians have the absolute right-of-way?
choices: Pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane
explanation: Pedestrians with a guide dog or a white cane have absolute right-of-way. Do not use your horn, because it could confuse or frighten them.

prompt: According to the Connecticut manual, how many motorcycles may share a single traffic lane?
choices: None; each needs its own lane
explanation: Motorcyclists may use a full lane, and two motorcycles may share a lane. Never pass a motorcycle in the same lane as it.

prompt: When must you report a crash to the police in Connecticut?
choices: If there is an injury, a death or property damage
Only if the other driver asks you to
explanation: You must report the accident to police if there is an injury, a death or property damage.

prompt: You back into a parked, unoccupied car in Connecticut and cannot find the owner. What should you do?
choices: Leave, since no one saw it
Leave a note where it can be seen with the date, time, and how to reach you
explanation: If the crash involves a parked vehicle, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a note where it can be seen with the date and time and how the owner can reach you.

prompt: You are pulled over by police at night in Connecticut. What does the manual recommend?
choices: Get out and walk to the officer
Turn on your interior light and keep your hands on the steering wheel
Search for your documents before the officer arrives
explanation: At night, turn on the interior light after stopping. Keep your hands on the wheel, keep doors closed, and get your license or registration only when asked.

prompt: Since October 1, 2025, who must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle in Connecticut?
explanation: Since October 1, 2025, Connecticut law requires motorcycle and motor-driven cycle operators and passengers under 21 (previously under 18) to wear protective headgear meeting federal standards. Permit holders must wear a helmet at any age.

prompt: A 35-year-old has a Connecticut motorcycle learner's permit. Must the rider wear a helmet?
choices: No, helmets are only required under 21
Yes, all motorcycle permit holders must wear a USDOT/NHTSA-approved helmet
explanation: Every motorcycle learner's permit holder, regardless of age, must wear USDOT or NHTSA approved protective headgear.

prompt: Which is allowed for a rider with a Connecticut motorcycle learner's permit?
choices: Riding during the day on local roads with a helmet
explanation: Permit holders may not ride on limited-access highways, at night, out of state, or with passengers. They must carry the permit and driver's license and wear an approved helmet.

prompt: How many questions are on Connecticut's motorcycle knowledge test?
explanation: The motorcycle knowledge exam has 16 questions taken from the Motorcycle Operator Manual and the Connecticut Driver's Manual.

prompt: A 20-year-old just received a Connecticut motorcycle endorsement. How long must the rider wait before carrying a passenger?
explanation: Riders 18 and older may not transport passengers for 90 days after getting a motorcycle endorsement. 16- and 17-year-olds must wait six months.

prompt: A 17-year-old just received a Connecticut motorcycle endorsement. How long must the rider wait before carrying a passenger?
explanation: No 16- or 17-year-old may carry a passenger on a motorcycle for six months after receiving a motorcycle endorsement.

prompt: Is lane splitting (riding between lanes of traffic) legal in Connecticut?
choices: No, a motorcycle may not be ridden between lanes of traffic
explanation: A motorcyclist may not ride between lanes of traffic or pass another motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle) in the same lane.

prompt: What is the maximum number of motorcycles that may ride side by side in a single lane in Connecticut?
explanation: A motorcycle is entitled to the full use of a lane, but operating more than two motorcycles abreast in a single lane is prohibited.

prompt: Under Connecticut law, when must a motorcycle operator wear goggles, glasses, or a face shield?
choices: Whenever riding, unless the motorcycle has an approved windshield or wind screen
explanation: Failing to wear approved goggles, glasses, or a face shield is an infraction, unless the motorcycle has a windshield or wind screen meeting state specifications.

prompt: For a motorcycle made after January 1, 1980, when must the headlight be on in Connecticut?
choices: At all times while riding on a highway
explanation: Anyone riding a motorcycle made after January 1, 1980 on a highway must keep the headlight on at all times.

prompt: What is the youngest age at which a person can get a Connecticut driver's license?
explanation: The legal age is 16 for both a learner's permit and a driver's license in Connecticut. Teens must also hold the permit for 120 or 180 days and finish the required training first.
ref: CT DMV teen driver's license page (portal.ct.gov)

prompt: Connecticut's teen passenger, curfew and cell-phone restrictions apply to licensed drivers of what ages?
choices: Only during the first year of driving, at any age
explanation: The restrictions apply to learner's permit holders and 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers, so they end when the driver turns 18. Adults 18 and older may use hands-free phones.

prompt: You are driving exactly at the posted speed limit on an icy road in Connecticut. Can you be ticketed for speeding?
choices: No, the posted limit is always legal
Yes, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for road conditions
Only if you cause a crash
explanation: Speed limits are set for ideal conditions. Even at the posted limit, you can get a ticket for traveling too fast for wet or icy roads, poor visibility, or heavy traffic.

prompt: Under normal conditions, what following distance does the Connecticut manual tell you to keep behind the vehicle ahead?
explanation: Use the three-second rule, which works at any speed. Increase to four seconds on slippery roads, in low visibility, when following motorcycles or large vehicles, or when pulling a trailer.

prompt: Which of these is a place where the Connecticut manual says you may NOT park?
choices: With your wheels 6 inches from the curb
In a marked space 40 feet from a stop sign
explanation: Never park on railroad tracks. Parking 15 feet from a hydrant is legal because the limit is 10 feet, and your wheels may be up to one foot from the curb.

prompt: A car comes toward you at night with its high beams on. According to the Connecticut Driver's Manual, what should you try first?
choices: Honk your horn to get the other driver's attention
Switch on your high beams until the other driver dims
Look directly at its headlights to judge its distance
Quickly flash your headlights a couple of times
explanation: The manual says to flash your headlights quickly a couple of times. If the driver still does not dim, look toward the right side of the road so you are not blinded, and never keep your own high beams on to get back at them.
